newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-DI MATTEO'S GOAL QUICKEST FOR 102 YEARS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-DI MATTEO'S GOAL QUICKEST FOR 102 YEARS.

text.p: Without surviving film footage and action replay evidence, no one can ever be certain, but there is little doubt that the early goal in the 1895 F.A. Cup final was scored in a quicker time than Roberto Di Matteo's opener for Chelsea on Saturday.
Repeated examination of video evidence following Chelsea's 2-0 win over Middlesbrough at Wembley Stadium shows that Di Matteo's shot crossed the goalline 42.4 seconds after kickoff.

It was the fastest Cup final goal since Jackie Milburn scored for Newcastle after 45 seconds when they beat Manchester City 3-1 in 1955, and was only the third time a goal had been scored in the first minute of a Wembley F.A. Cup final.
The only other occasion was when James Roscamp scored for Blackburn after 50 seconds when they beat Huddersfield 3-1 in 1928.

But the quickest Cup final goal in the competition's 126-year history was scored 102 years ago in 1895 when Aston Villa took the lead within 40 seconds of the kickoff against West Bromwich Albion at the old Crystal Palace. It was the only goal of the match.
Although there is no precise timing of the goal, all the surviving evidence places it as being scored between 30 and 40 seconds after the kickoff.

The only matter that will never be properly be resolved is which player actually scored it as it has been credited to both Villa inside forward Bob Chatt and centre forward John Devey in equal measure through the years.

The Official History of the F.A. Cup published in 1949 said the goal was scored "within the first 30 seconds" while a history of West Bromwich Albion publish in 1987 credited the goal to Chatt "after 39 seconds".
The Sunday Times of April 21, 1895, published the day after the final, credited the goal to Chatt "soon after the kickoff" but for many years the goal was also credited to Devey "after 30 seconds".
The Guiness Record of the F.A. Cup published in 1993 suggested the goal came nearer 40 seconds and that Chatt had probably scored it.

There was a strange postscript to that match five months later when Villa put the Cup on display in the window of a local shop in Birmingham where it was stolen on the night of September 11, 1895, and never recovered.
And it is a strange irony too to Di Matteo's goal, which is now the second fastest ever scored at Wembley in a first class match.
The fastest, after 38 seconds, came when England beat Yugoslavia 2-1 in a friendly on December 13, 1989. The scorer -- Bryan Robson, Middlesbrough's beaten manager on Saturday.
